**Routing rationale** — the deliverable is a contract-review-tier reading of a `skills/**` hunk. `skills/**` is governed surface, and only the `skills` (or `spec`) seat may spawn that tier. ⇒ the lane that owns the surface is the lane that can produce the deliverable. The filer's 「Suggested reader」 and the routing agree; ⭐ this is triage confirming it against the charter, ⛔ not deferring to the suggestion.

**p2 rationale, and ⛔ the reason it is not p3 despite not blocking a queue slot** — the card is right that PR #9400 is parked for a human merge and this review holds up no queue slot. But the gap is **tier coverage of record on a governed hunk that is waiting for a merge click**. The failure mode is a governed change landing with the compensating control never actually exercised — the out-of-tier seat did the honest half (built at default tier, handed the skills-face hunk over, scoped its ACCEPT to the code half) and the handover completes only when someone runs the tier. ⛔ Leaving it p3 invites it to be outrun by the merge it is supposed to precede.

⭐ **The filer did the structurally right thing and it is worth naming**: a cross-seat request is work, so it gets a card — ⛔ never a seat-post knock or a review note as its only carrier. That is exactly 「⛔ 座位贴敲门或裁决评论永不作跨座位请求的唯一载体」.

⚠️ **Carry this into the review, ⛔ do not lose it in the handover**: the rule's `❌ WRONG` example is `props: { title: … }`, a **non-predicate** key that is still silently dropped rather than refused. Correct and deliberate under the ruling (only the eight node-gate keys became loud) — but it means the example no longer demonstrates the half of the rule the rewritten sentence describes. That is a reviewer's judgement call and is the substantive question on this hunk, ⛔ not the +3 line count.

`Size/model suggestion:` S — one hunk, 6 added / 3 removed; the cost is the tier, ⛔ not the size.
